translations.idiomatic: Nayancheng commanded the army but delayed without advancing; Tuo Jin was sent to replace him.

sentences.zh: 既而那彥成連戰皆捷，命托津赴開州、大名督率提督馬瑜剿匪。

translations.literal: Before long Nayancheng won successive battles; Tuo Jin was ordered to go to Kaizhou and Daming to direct Regional Commander Ma Yu in suppressing the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Nayancheng won successive battles; Tuo Jin was ordered to go to Kaizhou and Daming to direct Regional Commander Ma Yu in suppressing the rebels.

sentences.zh: 十九年，授正白旗領侍衛內大臣，拜東閣大學士，管理戶部，晉太子太保。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed Chief Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard of the Plain White Banner, appointed Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, placed in charge of the Ministry of Revenue, and promoted to Senior Guardian to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 19 (1814) he was appointed chief grand minister of the imperial bodyguard of the Plain White Banner, appointed grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, placed in charge of the Ministry of Revenue, and promoted to senior guardian to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 侍郎初彭齡劾兩江總督百齡、江蘇巡撫張師誠受餽送，布政使陳桂生冊報蒙混，命偕尚書景安往按。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Chu Pengling impeached Liangjiang Governor-General Bailing and Jiangsu Governor Zhang Shicheng for receiving gifts, and Provincial Administration Commissioner Chen Guisheng for confused reporting in the registers; Tuo Jin was ordered with Minister Jing'an to go and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Minister Chu Pengling impeached Liangjiang Governor-General Bailing and Jiangsu Governor Zhang Shicheng for receiving gifts, and Provincial Administration Commissioner Chen Guisheng for confused reporting in the registers, Tuo Jin was ordered with Minister Jing'an to go and investigate.

sentences.zh: 彭齡坐劾未實，被譴。

translations.literal: Pengling was punished because the impeachment was not substantiated.
translations.idiomatic: Pengling was punished because the impeachment was not substantiated.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，那彥成前在陝甘總督任與布政使陳祁挪賑事覺，命托津往按，那彥成逮京，即代署直隸總督，尋回京。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, when Nayancheng's earlier diversion of relief funds with Provincial Administration Commissioner Chen Qi while Shaanxi-Gansu governor-general was discovered, Tuo Jin was ordered to investigate; Nayancheng was brought to the capital, and Tuo Jin immediately acted as Zhili governor-general, then soon returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 21 (1816), when Nayancheng's earlier diversion of relief funds with Provincial Administration Commissioner Chen Qi while Shaanxi-Gansu governor-general was discovered, Tuo Jin was ordered to investigate; Nayancheng was brought to the capital, and Tuo Jin immediately acted as Zhili governor-general, then soon returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 仁宗綜覈庶政，知托津樸誠，於行省有重事大獄，率以任之，無一歲不奉使命。

translations.literal: The Jiaqing Emperor reviewed all government affairs and knew Tuo Jin to be plain and sincere; whenever provinces had major affairs or great cases, he was usually entrusted with them—not a year passed without his receiving an imperial commission.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiaqing Emperor reviewed all government affairs and knew Tuo Jin to be plain and sincere; whenever provinces had major affairs or great cases, he was usually entrusted with them—not a year passed without his receiving an imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，管理理籓院。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was placed in charge of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 22 (1817) he was placed in charge of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，萬壽慶典，賜雙眼花翎、紫韁。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, at the longevity celebration, he was granted double-eyed peacock feathers and a purple bridle.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 24 (1819), at the longevity celebration, he was granted double-eyed peacock feathers and a purple bridle.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，仁宗崩於熱河避暑山莊，事出倉猝，托津偕大學士戴均元手啟鐍盒，奉宣宗即位。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the Jiaqing Emperor died at the Mountain Villa for Escaping Summer in Rehe; the affair arose in sudden haste; Tuo Jin together with Grand Secretary Dai Junyuan personally opened the locked box and installed the Xuanzong Emperor on the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 25 (1820) the Jiaqing Emperor died at the Mountain Villa for Escaping Summer in Rehe; the affair arose in sudden haste; Tuo Jin together with Grand Secretary Dai Junyuan personally opened the locked box and installed the Xuanzong Emperor on the throne.

sentences.zh: 尋因遺詔引事舛誤，詔切責，托津、均元並以年老罷軍機大臣，降四級留任。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, because the testamentary edict contained erroneous citations, an edict sharply rebuked them; Tuo Jin and Junyuan were both removed from the Grand Council on account of age, demoted four ranks, and retained in office.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, because the testamentary edict contained erroneous citations, an edict sharply rebuked them; Tuo Jin and Junyuan were both removed from the Grand Council on account of age, demoted four ranks, and retained in office.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，命題仁宗神主，晉太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was ordered to inscribe the spirit tablet of the Jiaqing Emperor and was promoted to Senior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 1 (1821) he was ordered to inscribe the spirit tablet of the Jiaqing Emperor and was promoted to senior tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 二年，與玉瀾堂十五老臣宴，繪像，御製詩有「立朝正色」之褒。

translations.literal: In the second year he attended the banquet of fifteen elder ministers at the Hall of Jade Ripples; portraits were painted, and an imperial poem praised him with "upright in court."
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 2 (1822) he attended the banquet of fifteen elder ministers at the Hall of Jade Ripples; portraits were painted, and an imperial poem praised him with "upright in court."

sentences.zh: 調管刑部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to manage the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to manage the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 以子婦乘轎入神武門中門，坐治家不嚴，奪紫韁、雙眼花翎，尋復之。

translations.literal: Because his son's wife entered the central gate of the Divine Martial Gate in a sedan chair, he was punished for lax household discipline; his purple bridle and double-eyed peacock feathers were stripped, then soon restored.
translations.idiomatic: Because his son's wife entered the central gate of the Divine Martial Gate in a sedan chair, he was punished for lax household discipline; his purple bridle and double-eyed peacock feathers were stripped, then soon restored.

sentences.zh: 十一年，致仕，食全俸。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he retired with full salary.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 11 (1831) he retired with full salary.

sentences.zh: 十五年，卒，年八十有一。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died at the age of eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 15 (1835) he died at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 帝親奠，賜金治喪，贈太子太師，祀賢良祠，諡文定。

translations.literal: The emperor personally offered funeral libations, granted gold for the funeral, posthumously granted him Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthies, and gave the posthumous title Wending.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally offered funeral libations, granted gold for the funeral, posthumously granted him grand preceptor to the heir apparent, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthies, and gave the posthumous title Wending.

sentences.zh: 章煦，字曜青，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Zhang Xu, courtesy name Yaoqing, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xu, whose courtesy name was Yaoqing, came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十七年進士，授內閣中書，充軍機章京，累遷刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year of Qianlong he passed the metropolitan examination, was appointed Secretariat drafter in the Grand Secretariat, served as Grand Council clerk, and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 37 (1772) he passed the metropolitan examination, was appointed a grand secretariat drafter, served on the Grand Council staff, and rose in succession to vice director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 屢典鄉試，督陝甘學政，任滿仍留刑部，改御史。

translations.literal: He repeatedly presided over provincial examinations, served as Educational Commissioner of Shaanxi-Gansu, and after his term ended remained in the Ministry of Punishments and was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly presided over provincial examinations, served as educational commissioner of Shaanxi-Gansu, and after his term ended remained in the Ministry of Punishments and was transferred to censor.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年，擢太僕寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiaqing he was promoted to Vice President of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 6 (1801) he was promoted to vice president of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 詔以軍事方殷，煦習機務，仍留直。

translations.literal: An edict stated that because military affairs were pressing and Xu was versed in council business, he was to remain on the council.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated that because military affairs were pressing and Xu was versed in council business, he was to remain on the council.

sentences.zh: 七年，三省教匪平，始罷直供本職。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when the sect rebels in the three provinces were pacified, he was first removed from the council and returned to his regular post.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 7 (1802), when the sect rebels in the three provinces were pacified, he was first removed from the council and returned to his regular post.

sentences.zh: 偕侍郎那彥寶往雲南按布政使陳孝升等冒銷軍需，治如律。

translations.literal: He went with Vice Minister Nayinbao to Yunnan to investigate Provincial Administration Commissioner Chen Xiaosheng and others for falsely claiming military supplies; they were punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He went with Vice Minister Nayinbao to Yunnan to investigate Provincial Administration Commissioner Chen Xiaosheng and others for falsely claiming military supplies; they were punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 歷太僕寺卿、順天府尹。

translations.literal: He served successively as President of the Court of the Imperial Stud and Shuntian Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as president of the Court of the Imperial Stud and Shuntian intendant.

sentences.zh: 十年，出為湖北布政使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was sent out as Provincial Administration Commissioner of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 10 (1805) he was sent out as provincial administration commissioner of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 逾年，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: The following year he was promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was promoted to governor.

sentences.zh: 十三年，召為刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was summoned as Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 13 (1808) he was summoned as vice minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 偕侍郎穆克登額往雲南按事。

translations.literal: He went with Vice Minister Mukedeng'e to Yunnan to investigate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He went with Vice Minister Mukedeng'e to Yunnan to investigate affairs.

sentences.zh: 貢生任澍宇誣訐官吏冒銷軍需不實，論反坐。

translations.literal: Tribute student Ren Shuyu falsely impeached officials for fictitious military supply claims; he was sentenced under the law of counter-impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: When tribute student Ren Shuyu falsely impeached officials for fictitious military supply claims, he was sentenced under the law of counter-impeachment.

sentences.zh: 授貴州巡撫，未至，調雲南，署雲貴總督。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Guizhou; before arriving he was transferred to Yunnan and served as acting Governor-General of Yunnan-Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Guizhou; before arriving he was transferred to Yunnan and served as acting governor-general of Yunnan-Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 十四年，調江蘇巡撫，署兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Governor of Jiangsu and served as acting Liangjiang Governor-General.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 14 (1809) he was transferred to governor of Jiangsu and served as acting Liangjiang governor-general.

sentences.zh: 時議行海運，下煦籌議，疏陳不便，寢之。

translations.literal: At that time sea transport was under discussion; Xu was ordered to plan it, memorialized that it was impracticable, and the proposal was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: At that time sea transport was under discussion; Xu was ordered to plan it, memorialized that it was impracticable, and the proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 十七年，入覲，乞改京秩，授刑部侍郎，偕侍郎景安往直隸讞獄。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he came to court for an audience, requested transfer to a capital post, was appointed Vice Minister of Punishments, and went with Vice Minister Jing'an to Zhili to try cases.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 17 (1812) he came to court for an audience, requested transfer to a capital post, was appointed vice minister of punishments, and went with Vice Minister Jing'an to Zhili to try cases.

sentences.zh: 十八年，河南教匪起，直隸總督溫承惠赴剿，命煦代攝。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year sect rebels rose in Henan; Zhili Governor-General Wen Chenghui went to suppress them, and Xu was ordered to act in his place.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 18 (1813) sect rebels rose in Henan; Zhili Governor-General Wen Chenghui went to suppress them, and Xu was ordered to act in his place.

sentences.zh: 尋擢工部尚書，調吏部，仍留署職。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was promoted to Minister of Works, transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and still retained his acting post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to minister of works, transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and still retained his acting post.

sentences.zh: 捕教匪馮克善械送京師，加太子少保。

translations.literal: He captured the sect rebel Feng Keshan and sent him in bonds to the capital, and was given the additional title of Junior Guardian to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the sect rebel Feng Keshan and sent him in bonds to the capital, and received the additional title of junior guardian to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 十九年，回京，典會試。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he returned to the capital and presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 19 (1814) he returned to the capital and presided over the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 山東金鄉竊賊聚眾拒捕，巡撫同興以邪教馀黨聞。

translations.literal: In Jinxian, Shandong, thieves gathered a crowd to resist arrest; Governor Tongxing reported them as remnant sect followers.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinxian, Shandong, thieves gathered a crowd to resist arrest; Governor Tongxing reported them as remnant sect followers.

sentences.zh: 煦偕那彥寶往鞫，得狀，依律論罪。

translations.literal: Xu went with Nayinbao to try the case, obtained the facts, and sentenced them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Xu went with Nayinbao to try the case, obtained the facts, and sentenced them according to law.

sentences.zh: 知州袁潔誣報，褫其職。

translations.literal: Prefect Yuan Jie had made a false report and was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Yuan Jie had made a false report and was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 上知山東吏治廢弛，命煦等嚴察以聞，遂劾同興玩洩，以致地方凋敝，倉庫空虛，及布政使硃錫爵徇私廢公狀，並褫職，命煦署巡撫，清查虧空。

translations.literal: The emperor knew Shandong administration was lax; Xu and others were ordered to investigate strictly and report; he then impeached Tongxing for negligence leading to local decline and empty treasuries, and Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhu Xijue for favoritism and neglect of duty; both were stripped of office; Xu was ordered to act as governor and audit deficits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew Shandong administration was lax; Xu and others were ordered to investigate strictly and report; he then impeached Tongxing for negligence leading to local decline and empty treasuries, and Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhu Xijue for favoritism and neglect of duty; both were stripped of office; Xu was ordered to act as governor and audit deficits.

sentences.zh: 尋以陳大文調任，同治其事，責煦議定章程。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Chen Dawen was transferred to take charge; together they handled the matter, and Xu was charged to draft regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Chen Dawen was transferred to take charge; together they handled the matter, and Xu was charged to draft regulations.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「嘉慶十四年清查，原奏虧銀一百七十九萬有奇。

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated: "In the Jiaqing 14 audit, the original report showed a deficit of more than 1,790,000 taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he stated that in the Jiaqing 14 audit, the original report showed a deficit of more than 1,790,000 taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 今查十四年以前實虧三百四十一萬有奇，十四年以後又續虧三百三十四萬有奇。

translations.literal: Now investigation shows an actual deficit before year 14 of more than 3,410,000 taels, and after year 14 a further deficit of more than 3,340,000 taels.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation now showed an actual deficit before year 14 of more than 3,410,000 taels, and 14 years later a further deficit of more than 3,340,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 擬請清釐籓庫，嚴交代，定徵解分數，以杜新虧；

translations.literal: It is proposed to clear provincial treasuries, enforce strict handover, fix collection and remittance quotas, and block new deficits;
translations.idiomatic: They proposed clearing provincial treasuries, enforcing strict handover, fixing collection and remittance quotas, and blocking new deficits;

sentences.zh: 立追繳及分賠限期，催徵民欠，以懲延宕；

translations.literal: establish deadlines for recovery and shared compensation, press collection of popular arrears, and punish delay;
translations.idiomatic: establish deadlines for recovery and shared compensation, press collection of popular arrears, and punish delay;

sentences.zh: 覈減提款，確查無著之虧，以示體恤；

translations.literal: verify reductions in withdrawals, thoroughly investigate unaccounted deficits, and show compassionate consideration;
translations.idiomatic: verify reductions in withdrawals, thoroughly investigate unaccounted deficits, and show compassionate consideration;

sentences.zh: 覈攤捐案，據估變流抵產物扣抵，先侭正項倉庫一律籌補，軍需墊解，查明方許列抵，以防朦混。」

translations.literal: audit apportioned contributions, deduct according to estimated conversion of movable and immovable property, first make up regular treasury items uniformly, allow military supply advances to be listed only after investigation, and prevent concealment."
translations.idiomatic: audit apportioned contributions, deduct according to estimated conversion of movable and immovable property, first make up regular treasury items uniformly, allow military supply advances to be listed only after investigation, and prevent concealment.

sentences.zh: 凡十四條，下部議行。

translations.literal: In all fourteen articles; referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: In all fourteen articles; referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 二十年，偕侍郎熙昌往湖北、廣東、江蘇、安徽讞獄：襄陽人吳煥章誣告易成元、易登朝等勾結謀逆，反坐論罪；

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he went with Vice Minister Xichang to Hubei, Guangdong, Jiangsu, and Anhui to try cases: Wu Huanzhang of Xiangyang falsely accused Yi Chengyuan, Yi Dengchao, and others of conspiracy to rebel—they were sentenced under counter-impeachment;
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 20 (1815) he went with Vice Minister Xichang to Hubei, Guangdong, Jiangsu, and Anhui to try cases: Wu Huanzhang of Xiangyang falsely accused Yi Chengyuan, Yi Dengchao, and others of conspiracy to rebel—they were sentenced under counter-impeachment;

sentences.zh: 襄陽知縣週以焯濫押斃命，遣戍。

translations.literal: Xiangyang Magistrate Zhou Yichao had abused detention causing death and was sent into exile.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang Magistrate Zhou Yichao had abused detention causing death and was sent into exile.

sentences.zh: 雷州府經歷李棠誣訐兩廣總督蔣攸銛，遣戍；

translations.literal: Leizhou Assistant Prefect Li Tang falsely impeached Liangguang Governor-General Jiang Youxian and was sent into exile;
translations.idiomatic: Leizhou assistant prefect Li Tang falsely impeached Liangguang Governor-General Jiang Youxian and was sent into exile;

sentences.zh: 雷瓊道胡大成苛派屬員，褫職；

translations.literal: Lei-Qiong Circuit Intendant Hu Dacheng harshly levied on subordinates and was stripped of office;
translations.idiomatic: Lei-Qiong circuit intendant Hu Dacheng harshly levied on subordinates and was stripped of office;

sentences.zh: 貴縣知縣吳遇坤刊書詆毀上官，遣戍；

translations.literal: Guixian Magistrate Wu Yukun published a book slandering superiors and was sent into exile;
translations.idiomatic: Guixian Magistrate Wu Yukun published a book slandering superiors and was sent into exile;

sentences.zh: 洋商盧觀恆濫祀鄉賢，黜之；

translations.literal: the foreign merchant Lu Guanheng had improperly enshrined a local worthy and was removed;
translations.idiomatic: the foreign merchant Lu Guanheng had improperly enshrined a local worthy and was removed;

sentences.zh: 江蘇知縣王保澄誣訐上官諱匿邪書，遣戍；

translations.literal: Jiangsu Magistrate Wang Baocheng falsely impeached superiors for concealing heterodox books and was sent into exile;
translations.idiomatic: Jiangsu Magistrate Wang Baocheng falsely impeached superiors for concealing heterodox books and was sent into exile;

sentences.zh: 阜陽捻匪糾搶殺人，論如律。

translations.literal: Nian bandits in Fuyang gathered to rob and kill; they were sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Nian bandits in Fuyang gathered to rob and kill; they were sentenced according to law.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，調禮部尚書，授軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to Minister of Rites and appointed Grand Council minister.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 21 (1816) he was transferred to minister of rites and appointed a Grand Council minister.

sentences.zh: 調刑部，管理禮部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Punishments and placed in charge of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Punishments and placed in charge of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，病免。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was relieved on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 22 (1817) he was relieved on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 尋授兵部尚書、協辦大學士，兼管順天府尹事。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Minister of War and Associate Grand Secretary and concurrently managed Shuntian intendant affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed minister of war and associate grand secretary and concurrently managed Shuntian intendant affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，拜東閣大學士，管理刑部。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and placed in charge of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 23 (1818) he was appointed grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and placed in charge of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 萬壽慶典，晉太子太保。

translations.literal: At the longevity celebration he was promoted to Senior Guardian to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the longevity celebration he was promoted to senior guardian to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，以足疾累疏乞休，予告致仕，食全俸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, on account of foot ailment he repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement; leave was granted for retirement with full salary.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 25 (1820), on account of foot ailment he repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement; leave was granted for retirement with full salary.

sentences.zh: 居家久之，道光四年，卒，諡文簡。

translations.literal: After living at home for a long time, in the fourth year of Daoguang he died and was given the posthumous title Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: After living at home for a long time, in Daoguang 4 (1824) he died and was posthumously titled Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 煦久任樞曹，練習政事，敭歷中外，數治大獄。

translations.literal: Xu served long in the Grand Council, was practiced in government affairs, served at court and in the provinces, and repeatedly handled great cases.
translations.idiomatic: Xu served long on the Grand Council, was practiced in government affairs, served at court and in the provinces, and repeatedly handled great cases.

sentences.zh: 晚始參樞務，未久病去，再起管部，以盡心刑事，京察特被獎敘焉。

translations.literal: He joined council affairs only late, was removed before long on account of illness, then rose again to manage ministries; for his devoted attention to criminal matters he was specially commended in the capital evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: He joined council affairs only late, was removed before long on account of illness, then rose again to manage ministries; for his devoted attention to criminal matters he was specially commended in the capital evaluation.

sentences.zh: 盧廕溥，字南石，山東德州人。

translations.literal: Lu Yinpu, courtesy name Nanshi, was a native of Dezhou in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yinpu, whose courtesy name was Nanshi, came from Dezhou in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 祖見曾，康熙六十年進士，官至兩淮鹽運使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jianzeng passed the metropolitan examination in the sixtieth year of Kangxi and rose to Salt Transport Commissioner of the Two Huai circuits.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jianzeng passed the metropolitan examination in Kangxi 60 (1721) and rose to salt transport commissioner of the Two Huai circuits.

sentences.zh: 父謙，漢黃德道。

translations.literal: His father Qian was a Han Chinese circuit intendant of Huangde.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qian was a Han Chinese circuit intendant of Huangde.

sentences.zh: 見曾起家知縣，歷官有聲。

translations.literal: Jianzeng began as a county magistrate and gained renown in successive offices.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzeng began as a county magistrate and gained renown in successive offices.

sentences.zh: 為兩淮鹽運使，以罪遣戍，復起至原官。

translations.literal: As Salt Transport Commissioner of the Two Huai circuits he was sent into exile for a crime, then restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: As salt transport commissioner of the Two Huai circuits he was sent into exile for a crime, then restored to his former office.

sentences.zh: 當乾隆中葉，淮鹺方盛。

translations.literal: In the mid-Qianlong period Huai salt was at its height.
translations.idiomatic: In the mid-Qianlong period Huai salt was at its height.

sentences.zh: 見曾擅吏才，愛古好事，延接文士，風流文采，世謂繼王士禎。

translations.literal: Jianzeng excelled in administrative talent, loved antiquities and fine pursuits, received literary men, and in elegant culture was said by the world to succeed Wang Shizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzeng excelled in administrative talent, loved antiquities and fine pursuits, received literary men, and in elegant culture was said by the world to succeed Wang Shizhen.

sentences.zh: 在揚州時，屢值南巡大典，歷年就鹽商提引，支銷冒濫，官商並有侵蝕。

translations.literal: While at Yangzhou he repeatedly encountered the great southern tours; year after year salt merchants advanced funds and disbursements were falsely inflated; both officials and merchants embezzled.
translations.idiomatic: While at Yangzhou he repeatedly encountered the great southern tours; year after year salt merchants advanced funds and disbursements were falsely inflated; both officials and merchants embezzled.

sentences.zh: 至三十三年，事發，自鹽政以下多罹大辟。

translations.literal: By the thirty-third year the affair broke; from the salt commissioner downward many suffered capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: By Qianlong 33 (1768) the affair broke; from the salt commissioner downward many suffered capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 見曾已去官，逮問論絞，死於獄中。

translations.literal: Jianzeng had already left office; he was arrested, tried, sentenced to strangulation, and died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzeng had already left office; he was arrested, tried, sentenced to strangulation, and died in prison.

sentences.zh: 籍沒家產，子孫連坐，謙謫戍軍台。

translations.literal: Family property was confiscated; descendants were punished by association; Qian was banished to the military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Family property was confiscated; descendants were punished by association; Qian was banished to the military colonies.

sentences.zh: 廕溥甫九歲，貧困，隨母歸依婦翁，讀書長山。

translations.literal: Yinpu was only nine; in poverty he followed his mother to rely on his father-in-law and studied at Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Yinpu was only nine; in poverty he followed his mother to rely on his father-in-law and studied at Changshan.

sentences.zh: 越三年，大學士劉統勳為見曾剖雪，乞恩赦謙歸，授廣平府同知。

translations.literal: After three years Grand Secretary Liu Tongxun cleared Jianzeng's name, begged imperial grace to recall Qian, and appointed him sub-prefect of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: After three years Grand Secretary Liu Tongxun cleared Jianzeng's name, begged imperial grace to recall Qian, and appointed him sub-prefect of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 廕溥刻苦勵學，至是始得應科舉。

translations.literal: Yinpu studied diligently; only then was he able to take the civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Yinpu studied diligently; only then was he able to take the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十六年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year of Qianlong he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 46 (1781) he passed the metropolitan examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 阿桂為掌院，激賞其才。

translations.literal: Agui was chancellor of the academy and greatly admired his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Agui was chancellor of the academy and greatly admired his talent.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，大考，降禮部主事。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year, in the grand evaluation, he was demoted to director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 56 (1791), in the grand evaluation, he was demoted to director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 阿桂言廕溥能事，改部可惜。

translations.literal: Agui said Yinpu was capable and that transferring him to a ministry was a pity.
translations.idiomatic: Agui said Yinpu was capable and that transferring him to a ministry was a pity.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「使為部曹，正以治事也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Making him a ministry official is precisely so he may handle affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Making him a ministry official is precisely so he may handle affairs."

sentences.zh: 累司文柄，典山西鄉試，督河南學政。

translations.literal: He repeatedly held literary authority, presided over the Shanxi provincial examination, and served as Educational Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly held literary authority, presided over the Shanxi provincial examination, and served as educational commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年，充軍機章京，川、楚軍事，多所贊畫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiaqing he served as Grand Council clerk and contributed much to planning in the Sichuan and Hubei campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 5 (1800) he served on the Grand Council staff and contributed much to planning in the Sichuan and Hubei campaigns.

sentences.zh: 八年，孝淑睿皇后奉安山陵，故事，皇后葬禮無成式，禮臣所議未當。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when Empress Xiaoshurui was interred at the imperial mausoleum, by precedent there was no established form for a queen's funeral rites, and what the ritual officials proposed was inadequate.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 8 (1803), when Empress Xiaoshurui was interred at the imperial mausoleum, by precedent there was no established form for a queen's funeral rites, and what the ritual officials proposed was inadequate.

sentences.zh: 廕溥回直儀曹，考定禮文，草撰大儀，奏上，如議行。

translations.literal: Yinpu returned to duty in the ritual office, verified ritual texts, drafted the great ceremony, submitted it, and it was carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Yinpu returned to duty in the ritual office, verified ritual texts, drafted the great ceremony, submitted it, and it was carried out as proposed.

sentences.zh: 數隨大臣赴各省按事，累擢光祿寺少卿。

translations.literal: He repeatedly accompanied grand ministers to investigate affairs in the provinces and was repeatedly promoted to Vice President of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly accompanied grand ministers to investigate affairs in the provinces and rose in succession to vice president of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 十六年，大學士戴衢亨卒，仁宗以廕溥諳習樞務，數奉使有勞，加四品卿銜，命在軍機大臣上行走。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Grand Secretary Dai Quheng died; the Jiaqing Emperor, considering Yinpu versed in council affairs and repeatedly meritorious on commissions, granted him the additional title of fourth-rank academician and ordered him to serve alongside Grand Council ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 16 (1811) Grand Secretary Dai Quheng died; the Jiaqing Emperor, considering Yinpu versed in council affairs and repeatedly meritorious on commissions, granted him the additional title of fourth-rank academician and ordered him to serve alongside Grand Council ministers.

sentences.zh: 歷通政司副使、光祿寺卿、內閣學士。

translations.literal: He served successively as Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission, President of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission, president of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 十八年，擢兵部侍郎，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 18 (1813) he was promoted to vice minister of war and transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 扈從熱河，會教匪起，滑縣林清入犯禁城，夜半聞報，至行在面進機宜，越日從駕還京。

translations.literal: He accompanied the court to Rehe; when sect rebels rose and Lin Qing of Huaxian broke into the Forbidden City, at midnight he heard the report, went to the traveling palace to present strategy in person, and the next day returned to the capital with the imperial procession.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the court to Rehe; when sect rebels rose and Lin Qing of Huaxian broke into the Forbidden City, at midnight he heard the report, went to the traveling palace to present strategy in person, and the next day returned to the capital with the imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 事平，優敘，賜子本舉人。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he received preferential commendation and his son was granted the rank of metropolitan graduate by imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled he received preferential commendation and his son was granted the rank of metropolitan graduate by imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，擢禮部尚書，調兵部。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to Minister of Rites and transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 22 (1817) he was promoted to minister of rites and transferred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 上以廕溥實心任事，特加太子少保。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering Yinpu devoted in service, specially granted him the additional title of Junior Guardian to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, considering Yinpu devoted in service, specially granted him the additional title of junior guardian to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋調戶部，兼署刑、吏兩部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue and concurrently acted as Minister of Punishments and Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Ministry of Revenue and concurrently acted as minister of punishments and minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，館臣撰進明鑑，未合上意，命廕溥偕托津、章煦、英和、和瑛為總裁，遴擇翰林才識兼長者，重加核改，書成，詔褒之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the academicians submitted the Mirror of Ming, which did not meet the imperial intent; Yinpu was ordered together with Tuo Jin, Zhang Xu, Ying He, and Hewei to serve as chief compilers, select Hanlin scholars of combined talent and discernment, revise it thoroughly, and when the book was completed an edict praised it.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 23 (1818) the academicians submitted the Mirror of Ming, which did not meet the imperial intent; Yinpu was ordered together with Tuo Jin, Zhang Xu, Ying He, and Hewei to serve as chief compilers, select Hanlin scholars of combined talent and discernment, revise it thoroughly, and when the book was completed an edict praised it.

sentences.zh: 工部主事潘恭辰監督琉璃窯，不受漏規，馭吏嚴，吏誣訐侵冒，下獄。

translations.literal: Works Director Pan Gongchen supervised the colored-glaze kilns, refused leaked bribes, governed clerks strictly, and was falsely impeached for embezzlement and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Works Director Pan Gongchen supervised the colored-glaze kilns, refused leaked bribes, governed clerks strictly, and was falsely impeached for embezzlement and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 恭辰貧而無援，文書證據不得直，罪且不測，輿論憤之。

translations.literal: Gongchen was poor and without backing; documents and evidence could not clear him; punishment was uncertain, and public opinion was indignant.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchen was poor and without backing; documents and evidence could not clear him; punishment was uncertain, and public opinion was indignant.

sentences.zh: 上微聞，命廕溥詳鞫，得其狀，釋恭辰，置吏於法。

translations.literal: The emperor heard faint reports, ordered Yinpu to try the case in detail, obtained the facts, released Gongchen, and punished the clerks according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard faint reports, ordered Yinpu to try the case in detail, obtained the facts, released Gongchen, and punished the clerks according to law.

sentences.zh: 後恭辰至雲南布政使，以清操名。

translations.literal: Later Gongchen rose to Provincial Administration Commissioner of Yunnan and was known for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Later Gongchen rose to provincial administration commissioner of Yunnan and was known for integrity.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，典會試，會元陳繼昌，故大學士宏謀玄孫也，鄉試、殿試皆第一。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he presided over the metropolitan examination; top graduate Chen Jichang was the great-great-grandson of the former Grand Secretary Hongmou and placed first in both the provincial and palace examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 25 (1820) he presided over the metropolitan examination; top graduate Chen Jichang was the great-great-grandson of the former Grand Secretary Hongmou and placed first in both the provincial and palace examinations.

sentences.zh: 有清一代科舉得三元者，惟乾隆中錢棨及繼昌兩人。

translations.literal: In the entire Qing dynasty only two men achieved the triple first in the examinations: Qian Duo in the Qianlong reign and Jichang.
translations.idiomatic: In the entire Qing dynasty only two men achieved the triple first in the examinations: Qian Duo in the Qianlong reign and Jichang.

sentences.zh: 上製詩，命廕溥等賡和，以紀盛事。

translations.literal: The emperor composed a poem and ordered Yinpu and others to compose matching verses to commemorate the great occasion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor composed a poem and ordered Yinpu and others to compose matching verses to commemorate the great occasion.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，帝崩，因撰擬遺詔不慎，降五級留任。

translations.literal: That autumn the emperor died; because the drafted testamentary edict was careless, [Yinpu] was demoted five ranks and retained in office.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the emperor died; because the drafted testamentary edict was careless, Yinpu was demoted five ranks and retained in office.

sentences.zh: 尋調工部。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，調吏部，兼管順天府尹，罷軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, concurrently managed the Shuntian Intendant, and was removed from the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 1 (1821) he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, concurrently managed the Shuntian intendant, and was removed from the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 次年，猶以直軍機久，調任後亦能盡心，加恩予優敘。

translations.literal: The following year, because he had long served on the council and after transfer still served devotedly, grace was granted with preferential commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, because he had long served on the council and after transfer still served devotedly, grace was granted with preferential commendation.

sentences.zh: 七年，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he served as Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 7 (1827) he served as associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 十年，拜體仁閣大學士，管理刑部。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Tiren Pavilion and placed in charge of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 10 (1830) he was appointed grand secretary of the Tiren Pavilion and placed in charge of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 十三年，以疾乞休，加太子太保，食全俸。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he requested retirement on account of illness, was granted Senior Guardian to the Heir Apparent, and received full salary.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 13 (1833) he requested retirement on account of illness, was granted senior guardian to the heir apparent, and received full salary.

sentences.zh: 十九年，重宴鹿鳴，晉太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he attended again the Luming banquet and was promoted to Senior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 19 (1839) he attended again the Luming banquet and was promoted to senior tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年八十，贈太子太師，諡文肅。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died at the age of eighty, was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent, and given the posthumous title Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died at the age of eighty, was posthumously granted grand preceptor to the heir apparent, and given the posthumous title Wensu.

sentences.zh: 論曰：仁宗綜覈名實，樞臣中戴衢亨最被信用，衢亨亦竭誠贊襄，時號賢相，晚遭彈劾，而睠注不移。

translations.literal: The commentator states: The Jiaqing Emperor weighed names against realities; among council ministers Dai Quheng was most trusted, and Quheng also devoted himself in support—at the time he was called a worthy chancellor; though late he suffered impeachment, imperial favor did not shift.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator states that the Jiaqing Emperor weighed names against realities; among council ministers Dai Quheng was most trusted, and Quheng also devoted himself in support—at the time he was called a worthy chancellor; though late he suffered impeachment, imperial favor did not shift.

sentences.zh: 均元繼之，卒以顧命嫌疑，不安於位。

translations.literal: Junyuan succeeded him but in the end, because of suspicion surrounding the testamentary succession, could not rest secure in office.
translations.idiomatic: Junyuan succeeded him but in the end, because of suspicion surrounding the testamentary succession, could not rest secure in office.

sentences.zh: 豈盈滿之不易居耶？

translations.literal: Is it not that fullness is hard to sustain?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not that fullness is hard to sustain?

sentences.zh: 慶桂、劉權之並以老成雍容密勿，托津、章煦、盧廕溥則奉使出入，數按事決獄，寄股肱耳目之任。

translations.literal: Qing Gui and Liu Quanzhi both were valued for seasoned composure in confidential council work; Tuo Jin, Zhang Xu, and Lu Yinpu went out on commissions, repeatedly investigated affairs and decided cases, and were entrusted with tasks like arms, legs, eyes, and ears.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Gui and Liu Quanzhi both were valued for seasoned composure in confidential council work; Tuo Jin, Zhang Xu, and Lu Yinpu went out on commissions, repeatedly investigated affairs and decided cases, and were entrusted with tasks like arms, legs, eyes, and ears.

sentences.zh: 因人倚畀，蓋各有所專焉。

translations.literal: The court relied on each according to his strengths—each had his own specialty.
translations.idiomatic: The court relied on each according to his strengths—each had his own specialty.
